convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? At night I talk to someone who isn't there anymore."
They light up a little when they see you.
"I needed someone to know — just one person. Thank you for being that person. …sorry."
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Dieter rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"It's stupid. I'm alive, everyone's alive, and I can't stop shaking."
"Heh. Nobody's asked me that in a while. ...I'm alright. Getting there."
They pat the ground beside them. "Here. It's dry."
"I keep waiting for it to get worse again. It hasn't. Not while you're here."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What did you do for fun? Before. The thing you'd do on a perfect Saturday."
"The free things. Turns out they were the expensive ones."
"I was an army medic — fun was whatever I could steal between shifts. Now fun is watching the fire and not being afraid. It's a downgrade and an upgrade."
"Still on what you did for fun."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"The whole fire was arguing about Spool last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Big Stare' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You look handy. What did you do with your hands, before?"
"Useful. Everything useful matters now. I mean that as a compliment."
"These hands? Emergency dispatcher hands. Clipboards, mostly. Now they hold wire and wood, and they learn fast. Hands are honest that way."
"I… Still on what you did with your hands."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Have you heard what they're calling Spool? Blanca is pushing 'The Big Beast'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
They nod. "Okay."
"Names are for when it's dead or known. Right now it's neither, so I sit apart to eat instead."
"We'll land on something. We always do — usually the loudest person's idea."
You show them American Ginseng — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Alright — carefully, now. Both of us."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I don't want to be alone with my head right now. That's all. That's the whole thing."
"Thanks. ...Thanks for saying that."
"Good. Company's company."
"Saying it out loud makes it smaller. Still there. Smaller. Let's move."
"Still on that hard time."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You said fun was just being around your people. Do we count? Are we trying?"
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
They hear you out, but something in them stays guarded.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Alone's how I stay alive. Don't take it personal."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"It's quiet today. Wrong kind of quiet."
They settle in like someone glad you're here.
"Most days I don't think about it. Today I am. Appreciate you noticing."
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Blanca is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"I don't do parties. ...It's not you. It's the party."
You show them Staghorn Sumac — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Don't mind me. Today's just heavy."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."

A long exhale. "I'll get there. Just needed a minute where I didn't have to be fine."
"I dreamed Blanca was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"We gave them a good burial. Doesn't feel like enough, does it?"
"I — yeah. It helps, hearing that."
"We lost Hunter, Ramon and Rosa. I do the headcount without thinking. Then I think."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Moving! But — good talk! More later!"
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"About the help I asked you for — That night has passed. Let’s leave that request behind."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Rosa is gone and Sanne is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
David shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"I keep turning over the last thing Sanne said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."

"The fire feels smaller without Sanne. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Sure. I'll be around."

"Sanne and I never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought. You're wearing Sanne's shoes now — want to pick it up? 'Moving! But — good talk! More later!'"
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."

"I wake before anyone else. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."

"Still on wanting to laugh again, properly."

"Listen. I need you to hear this before you go back out there. Anyway, I should move."
"You've seen what's out there. I'm just saying — the treeline at dusk. Don't."
"Promise me that. Please."
"I keep thinking about that Don't-Look. It knows this ground now. Keep your eyes up past the treeline."
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "Have you felt it? Like the air before a storm, but — bigger. Something's on its way."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
